reconcile_note: Every cgiFormString value read by cig_portforwording_del (the auStack_236, auStack_20, var_28h, uStack_30 and acStack_234 buffers) reaches only the callee at 0x00008ffc, which is safe_system_nonblock. That callee packs its varargs into a discrete argv[] array and calls safe_exec, which fork()s and calls execvp(argv0, argv). There is no shell string on this path, so cgi metacharacters stay literal argv elements. The only raw system() call takes the fixed constant *0x0000c408 = "killall -1 asaeiiim >/dev/null", with no cgi value spliced in. The sprintf results (format string *0x0000c40c and its siblings) feed only xml_del / xml_set_str / xml_write_file config writes, never a command. No injectable command path exists, so the terminal is not-vulnerable. This verdict is auth-independent: the attacker input never reaches the shell, so it is not a command injection regardless of whether the path is authenticated. The upstream session check sym.check_login (0xe2b4) gates this handler, so the requested command runs only for a request that already holds a valid session.
